commitResults.messageBody: Add Todo, Deadline, and Event task types using inheritance. Parse typed commands and preserve task-specific details when listing, marking, and unmarking tasks. Include the project-local visual diff skill used to review changes.

Add Mochi-specific exception handling for empty descriptions, unknown commands, malformed task syntax, and invalid task numbers. Preserve chatbot state and continue accepting commands after recoverable input errors.

commitResults.messageTitle: Implement Level 8 date and time support

commitResults.messageBody:
The Java sources contain inconsistent formatting and incomplete API
documentation, making the code harder to read and review.

Standardize naming, imports, switch indentation, and JavaDoc throughout
the production code. This keeps the codebase consistent with the course
coding conventions without changing application behavior.

Java changes need a consistent project-specific standard so future edits
do not reintroduce style deviations.

Add a reusable SE-EDU Java coding skill and require agents to load it for
all Java work. This keeps the rules discoverable and enforceable in the
repository.

Commit messages and branch names need a shared project standard so future
history remains consistent and easy to review.

Add a reusable SE-EDU Git skill and require agents to apply it whenever
they propose or create commits and branches. This records the convention
where future contributors can discover it.

The JavaDoc and coding-standard branches both update public APIs,
creating overlapping documentation and formatting changes.

Combine the JavaDoc coverage with SE-EDU formatting updates, and add the
project-local Java and Git standard skills. This preserves documentation
while enforcing the standards for future work.

The Level 9 branch adds task search while the JavaDoc and coding-
standard merges update the same command-processing classes.

Combine the find command with the documented, standards-compliant code.
Preserve parser validation, description-only matching, and text-UI
coverage.

Add the tutorial-style JavaFX entry point and FXML chat interface.

Route GUI input through Mochi's existing command-processing path while
preserving the text UI and persistence behavior.

Mochi only supports interaction through the command-line interface.

A graphical interface makes the application easier to interact with and
satisfies the Level-10 GUI requirement.

Add a JavaFX interface that allows users to enter commands and view
Mochi's responses in an application window.

Several components rely on assumptions established by earlier parsing
and validation steps.

Add assertions to document these internal invariants and detect
programming errors during development. Keep normal exception handling
for invalid user input and malformed stored data.

Task descriptions do not change after construction, and subclasses do
not need direct field access.

Restrict the field to Task and make it immutable. This reduces its scope
and prevents accidental mutation while preserving access through the
existing getter.

Parser.parse mixes input tokenization with dispatching commands
that have arguments, making its main flow longer and less consistent
in abstraction.

Extract argument-based dispatch into a focused method and use a switch
for missing-argument categories. This makes the parsing path easier to
scan and avoids compound condition chains.

Storage.parseTask combines field validation, task reconstruction, and
status restoration in one long method. This makes the successful parsing
path harder to identify and mixes multiple abstraction levels.

Extract validation, field-count lookup, and task creation into
focused methods. Keep parseTask as a readable sequence of the main
reconstruction steps while preserving malformed-data handling.

The full-list and matching-list responses duplicate the same
numbering and formatting loop. The full-list version also requests a
fresh task snapshot during every iteration.

Extract the shared formatting into one helper and give the TaskList
parameter a singular name. This removes duplication and makes each
public response method state only what differs.

Task filtering currently uses explicit iteration even though the
operation is a simple transformation over a collection.

Use a Java Stream to express the filtering logic more directly while
preserving the existing behavior.

Some commands require longer keywords even when the intended action is
unambiguous.

Add short aliases for common commands while preserving all existing
command syntax. This makes frequent commands faster to enter without
breaking backward compatibility.
Add assertions for internal invariants

Preserve the CodeQuality refactoring of task reconstruction while
incorporating the latest changes from master.

This avoids duplicating completion-status handling and keeps Storage
responsibilities separated clearly.
Branch a code quality

Integrate the latest Assertions and CodeQuality changes from master while preserving the Streams implementation.

This keeps the Streams branch current before merging it back into master.
Use streams for task filtering
